attributes.body:
から can have several different meanings in Japanese, depending on which part of the sentence it is in, and what comes before/after it. It is often translated as 'because', or 'since'. In these cases, it just means 'Because of (A), (B)'.

から may be used with almost any type of word, but when the nuance is 'because', it will require だ before it when following a noun or な-Adjective.

Despite having several different nuances, it may be easier to think of から as meaning 'from' in all situations, as that is the base nuance.

From (A as a reason), (B) = Because/Since.

From (A as a location), (B) = From.

Fun Fact

から is a special type of particle in Japanese called a case marking particle. These are particles that describe the relationship that (A) and (B) exist in. We will learn more about these soon!

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Using から (because) with nouns, adjectives and verbs
Expressing reason or causation using 「から」 and 「ので」
BECAUSE (から vs ので, からです vs ですから)

attributes.body: から expresses a reason or cause, similar to 'because' or 'so' in English, with the structure (A) から (B). In contrast, ものだから is more emphatic or emotional, often used to explain or justify actions. Both can be used in subjective statements, where the speaker presents their perspective or judgment.

Both したがって and から express a cause or reason. The difference is that から is common in casual, everyday speech, while したがって is more formal, used in writing or structured speech. Additionally, から appears in the middle of a sentence, while したがって comes at the start. To use から at the start, you would use ですから or だから.

Both から and ものですから・もので express reasons or explanations. から is more straightforward and commonly used, similar to '(A), so (B)' in English. ものですから・もので places more emphasis on the reason, often used to explain one's own actions. Note that ものですから is more polite, while から is used in more casual speech.

second_relatable.title: ものですから・もので
second_relatable.meaning: Because, My excuse is, My explanation is

attributes.body: から expresses a reason or cause, similar to 'because of A, B' or 'A, so B' in English. The reason comes before から, with the result after. からこそ is the same から followed by the emphatic こそ, highlighting that the given reason is precisely or solely responsible for what follows. It's used for strong arguments or emphatic points.

Both から and なぜなら〜から express reasons or causes. から is straightforward and casual, used in both casual conversations and formal speech, similar to 'A, so B.' In contrast, なぜなら〜から emphasizes the reason more strongly, often used in writing or formal speech with the nuance of 'As for why, it's because...' and typically when explaining a point in detail.

second_relatable.title: なぜなら〜から
second_relatable.meaning: Because, The reason is, That is because

attributes.body: Both し～し and から express reasons, similar to 'so' or 'because' in English. The reason (A) for outcome (B) is always followed by し or から, e.g. (A) し/から (B). The key difference is that から focuses on a single reason, while し～し lists multiple reasons. Even with one reason, し implies other unstated or implied reasons.

から and ので both express a cause or reason, similar to the English 'A, so B.' The reason comes first, followed by から or ので, and then the result. から is more colloquial, used in everyday speech, and often for personal or emotional statements. ので is slightly more formal and tends to be used for more objective statements.

second_relatable.title: ので
second_relatable.meaning: Because, So, Since, The reason being

attributes.body: から expresses a cause or reason, similar to 'A, so B' in English. もの or もん (with もん being more casual) can also express an emphatic or emotional reason, similar to 'because' in English. The main difference is that から can be used mid-sentence, while もの or もん typically appears at the end of a sentence and conveys a more personal or emotional tone.
